instructions.title: How you are when you're close to someone
paragraphs: These questions are about how you tend to be in romantic relationships in general — across the ones you've had, not one in particular. It matters that you answer generally, because that's what makes the result mean something.
If you're not seeing anyone at the moment, answer as you usually are when you're close to someone. If you've had little relationship experience, answer as you think you'd be — that's useful too.
There are no right answers, and nothing here is a diagnosis. It takes about five minutes.

items.text: The possibility of being left stays somewhere in my mind.
I brace myself for relationships ending, even when things are going well.
I don't spend much time wondering whether a relationship will last.
I suspect I put more into relationships than the other person does.
I assume that someone who chooses to be with me means it.
When someone tells me they care about me, I take it at face value.
I look for signs that things between us are still all right.
I pick up quickly on any change in how warm someone is towards me.
I can go a good while without needing any particular sign that things are fine.
When something feels unresolved with someone close to me, it takes over my thinking.
A short silence from someone I'm close to can stay with me for hours.
When a message goes unanswered, I get on with my day.
When I sense someone pulling back, I press harder to close the distance.
If someone needs space, I can give it without needing things settled first.
When I'm unsure where I stand, I can sit with that rather than seek an answer straight away.
I expect that if someone saw all of me, they'd think less of me.
How a partner is treating me doesn't much change how I feel about myself.
Someone who got to know me properly would like what they found.
I get uneasy when someone wants to be very close to me emotionally.
I'd rather keep a certain distance, even with someone I love.
I'm comfortable being emotionally close to a partner.
There are things about me I'd keep from a partner indefinitely.
I'm comfortable letting a partner see me at my lowest.
I say what I'm actually feeling to the person I'm with.
I'd sooner deal with a difficulty on my own than take it to a partner.
Leaning on a partner for something important doesn't come easily to me.
When something's gone wrong, going to my partner is my first instinct.
Being looked after makes me want to change the subject.
I can accept help from a partner without feeling I owe something.
I like being taken care of when I'm unwell or struggling.
When things get tense between us, my instinct is to go quiet.
Under pressure in a relationship, I withdraw before I explain.
When there's friction, I'd rather stay in the room and work it out.
The idea of two lives becoming fully entwined makes me uneasy.
I like the feeling of my life being bound up with someone else's.
Building something jointly with a partner appeals to me more than keeping things separate.
